newsitem.title: UK: Four held in beating death of N.Ireland policeman.
newsitem.headline: Four held in beating death of N.Ireland policeman.

text.p: Four men were ordered held in custody on Wednesday charged with murdering an off-duty Northern Ireland police officer who was kicked to death by a mob.
One of the accused was the son of a part-time policeman, according to security sources.
The killing, blamed by media reports on pro-British Protestants, intensified tension in Northern Ireland, which has been shaken recently by rival guerrilla violence and sectarian bitterness.

During a brief court hearing in Coleraine, County Londonderry, a detective said the four men had replied "not guilty" when the charges were put to them. The magistrate ordered them held pending another hearing on June 20.

Gregory Taylor, 41, a father of three, was set upon in a street in the town of Ballymoney on Sunday by a mob angry that police had banned Protestant parades from passing through a nearby Roman Catholic village, media reports said.
In London, Prime Minister Tony Blair told parliament he abhorred Taylor's murder.
"It was absolutely appalling, it was totally unprovoked and it was precisely the example of the type of random, vicious violence that we want to stop," he said.
He said the policeman's killing underlined the importance of giving impetus to the multi-party peace talks about the future of Northern Ireland that resumed in Belfast on Tuesday.

The killing, the latest in a series of street attacks by Protestant and Catholic gangs, has increased fears about the potential for violence during contentious pro-British parades over the next few weeks.
Northern Ireland's majority Protestants strongly support continued rule from London. The Catholic minority want an all-Ireland state ruled from Dublin.
